newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati Milacron sees EPS, sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati Milacron sees EPS, sales growth.

text.p: Cincinnati Milacron Inc said on Tuesday that it will be well positioned to meet or exceed its earnings per share and sales targets, if the company's businesses in Europe improve in the second half.

"If Europe does pick up in the second half, Milacron will be well positioned to meet or exceed our annual targets of seven percent to eight percent sales growth and 15 percent or greater increases in earnings per share," chairman and chief executive Daniel Meyer said in a statement.
If the rebound in Europe is delayed, the company expects some growth in its results, but it will not be as strong.

Cincinnati Milacron said that the company's outlook in North America and Asia remained positive but it was premature to be optimistic about Europe. There are preliminary signs that conditions in Europe may be improving, the company said.

Meyer said that Milacron was an active participant in all three large global markets and planned to increase its market share through extensive new product introductions and aggressive sales force expansions.
In the Cincinnati Milacron's first quarter, plastics machinery had $149 million in sales in the quarter, up from $123 million a year ago.
Operating earnings in the segment fell to $9.2 million, including a $3.5 million pretax operating loss by the company's injection molding subsidiary in Germany, from $10.7 million.

Machine tool sales in the first quarter increased by 11 percent to $90 million from $81 million a year ago, since the aerospace industry continued to show strength, the company said. Operating earnings doubled to $1.8 million for the quarter, the company said.

First quarter industrial products sales of $139 million declined seven percent from $150 million a year ago. Sales were hurt by currency translations and continued weakness in the European market, Cincinnati Milacron said. Operating earnings in the segment were flat at $16.6 million in the quarter, the company said.
